Cold Case Review File 1984-0912 (Harbor Auto Body Homicide).
[doc02 — Witness Interview, Marcus Vance, 1984-10-14]: "I locked up the paint bay at 8:30 PM on Friday, drove my blue Chevelle straight to the Bowl-A-Rama on 4th, and bowled three league games until midnight."
[doc11 — Harbor Power & Light Time-Step Submeter Log, Bay 3]: "1984-10-12 21:42:00 — 240V Compressor & Downdraft Booth Breaker Engaged (38.4 Amps continuous draw until 22:19:00)."
[doc14 — Bowl-A-Rama Friday Night Scratch League Score Sheet]: "Team 4 (M. Vance): Marked ABSENT / BLIND SCORE (135-135-135) for Frames 1-10, Games 1 through 3."
Audit Vance's Friday night alibi against the archival records.

CASE BLUF: Two independent archival records contradict Marcus Vance's stated timeline and location between 20:30 and 24:00 on 1984-10-12.

1. CONTRADICTION (Shop Departure vs. Electrical Load): In doc02, Vance states, "I locked up the paint bay at 8:30 PM on Friday, drove my blue Chevelle straight to the Bowl-A-Rama on 4th." However, doc11 logs active industrial machinery draw in Bay 3 over an hour later: "1984-10-12 21:42:00 — 240V Compressor & Downdraft Booth Breaker Engaged (38.4 Amps continuous draw until 22:19:00)."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Another employee with a shop key entered Bay 3 after Vance departed at 20:30, or the compressor pressure switch suffered an air-line leak and cycled on automatically while a timer-controlled exhaust fan engaged.

2. CONTRADICTION (Bowling League Attendance): In doc02, Vance claims he "bowled three league games until midnight." In contrast, doc14 records: "Team 4 (M. Vance): Marked ABSENT / BLIND SCORE (135-135-135) for Frames 1-10, Games 1 through 3."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Vance arrived at the bowling alley late or drank in the lounge and bowled open-play frames on a non-league lane after his team had already locked in his blind score.

3. NEXT LEAD:
   - Pull the 1984 Bowl-A-Rama bar tab register and interview Team 4 captain regarding whether Vance appeared at the lanes at any point on 1984-10-12.
   - Re-interview Marcus Vance anchored to doc14: "The Friday Night Scratch League score sheet (doc14) lists you as ABSENT / BLIND SCORE for all three games; which lane did you bowl on, and who signed your score sheet?"

Intake Memo — Case 1996-CR-4401 (St. Jude Infirmary Pharmacist Death). Please run a cross-examiner check on nurse supervisor Helen Krol's statement.
- EX-04 (Sworn Deposition of Helen Krol, 1996-02-19): "I never left the 4th-floor pediatric wing between 01:00 and 04:00 AM. I was charting at the central station the whole shift and didn't go near the basement narcotics vault."
- EX-17 (Simplex Badge Reader Audit Trail, Door B-09 Basement Pharmacy): "1996-02-17 02:18:44 — Badge #0419 (ASSIGNED: KROL, HELEN R.) — ACCESS GRANTED."
- EX-19 (4th Floor Narcotics Pyxis Dispenser Tape): "02:14:02 to 02:41:10 — ZERO transactions logged under operator ID HKROL; terminal idle."

CASE BLUF: Electronic access logs contradict Helen Krol's sworn deposition placing her exclusively on the 4th floor during the 01:00–04:00 window.

1. CONTRADICTION (Basement Vault Access): In EX-04, Krol states, "I never left the 4th-floor pediatric wing between 01:00 and 04:00 AM... and didn't go near the basement narcotics vault." EX-17 directly records: "1996-02-17 02:18:44 — Badge #0419 (ASSIGNED: KROL, HELEN R.) — ACCESS GRANTED" at Door B-09 Basement Pharmacy.
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Krol loaned Badge #0419 to a float nurse or pharmacy runner for an emergency medication pickup, or her badge was misplaced/cloned earlier in the shift.

2. CORROBORATING GAP (4th Floor Station Activity): Krol's claim in EX-04 that she "was charting at the central station the whole shift" is uncorroborated during a 27-minute gap in EX-19 ("02:14:02 to 02:41:10 — ZERO transactions logged under operator ID HKROL; terminal idle").
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Krol was completing handwritten paper flowsheets at the nursing desk rather than interacting with the electronic Pyxis dispenser during that 27-minute interval.

3. NEXT LEAD:
   - Pull handwritten 4th-floor pediatric patient vitals charts for 02:00–03:00 on 1996-02-17 to verify ink entries and timestamps signed by Krol.
   - Re-interview Helen Krol anchored to EX-17: "Badge #0419 registered ACCESS GRANTED at Door B-09 Basement Pharmacy at 02:18:44 (EX-17); was your badge in your possession throughout the 1996-02-17 night shift, or did anyone else carry it?"

Bates #00412–#00429 | Monongahela Rail Yard Arson-Homicide (2003-11-04)
Bates #00412 (Statement of Brakeman Roy Tatum): "I was stuck in caboose #88 on the north siding from 11:00 PM till 1:30 AM waiting on the air brake test. My cell phone was dead, so I didn't call anyone."
Bates #00419 (Cingular Wireless CDR, MSISDN 412-555-0193 registered to R. Tatum): "2003-11-04 23:47:12 — Outbound call to 412-555-0844, duration 184s, Cell Site 309-Sector 2 (Azimuth 140 deg, covering South Fuel Depot, 4.2 miles south of North Siding)."
Bates #00429 (Yardmaster Switch Log): "Caboose #88 coupled and cleared North Siding outbound at 22:50:00."

CASE BLUF: Cellular call detail records and the yardmaster switch log contradict Roy Tatum's account of both his location on the north siding and the status of his cell phone on 2003-11-04.

1. CONTRADICTION (Phone Status & Location Sector): In Bates #00412, Tatum states, "I was stuck in caboose #88 on the north siding from 11:00 PM till 1:30 AM... My cell phone was dead, so I didn't call anyone." Bates #00419 logs an active call from his handset during that window: "2003-11-04 23:47:12 — Outbound call to 412-555-0844, duration 184s, Cell Site 309-Sector 2 (Azimuth 140 deg, covering South Fuel Depot, 4.2 miles south of North Siding)."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Tatum left his cell phone inside a crew pickup truck or locker near the South Fuel Depot where another rail worker placed the outbound call, or his handset battery briefly recovered enough charge to place one call while RF propagation anomaly/load-shedding handed the call to Cell Site 309-Sector 2.

2. CONTRADICTION (Caboose #88 Movement): Tatum's statement in Bates #00412 that he was inside caboose #88 on the north siding starting at 11:00 PM conflicts with Bates #00429: "Caboose #88 coupled and cleared North Siding outbound at 22:50:00."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Tatum misremembered the caboose unit number on the north siding, or the yardmaster switch log clock was running 15–20 minutes fast and Tatum rode caboose #88 south toward the fuel depot.

3. NEXT LEAD:
   - Subpoena subscriber identity and toll records for destination number `412-555-0844` cited in Bates #00419.
   - Interview the locomotive engineer and conductor assigned to the 22:50 outbound consist in Bates #00429 to establish who was aboard Caboose #88.

File 2011-0083 (Prairie Grain Co-op Silo Fall / Homicide).
doc04 (Interview with Co-op Manager Dale Sutter, 2011-08-22): "I was in Omaha at the Cornhusker Marriott the whole weekend of August 19th–21st. Checked in Friday afternoon, never left the downtown area until checkout Sunday at noon."
doc08 (Cornhusker Marriott Folio #88219): "Guest: D. Sutter. Check-in: 2011-08-19 15:12. Keycard Lock Audit Room 614: Last entry 2011-08-19 18:04; zero door openings logged 2011-08-20; next entry 2011-08-21 09:40."
doc12 (Kansas Turnpike / I-80 Fuel Mart Receipt Found in Co-op F-250 Glovebox): "2011-08-20 22:15 — York, NE (Exit 353, 8 miles from Prairie Grain Co-op) — 26.4 gal Diesel, Fleet Card #004-SUTTER, PIN verified."

CASE BLUF: Hotel keycard telemetry and a PIN-verified fleet fuel purchase 8 miles from the crime scene contradict Dale Sutter's claim that he remained in downtown Omaha all weekend.

1. CONTRADICTION (Weekend Presence in Omaha vs. York Fuel Purchase): In doc04, Sutter states he "never left the downtown area until checkout Sunday at noon." However, doc12 places his PIN-verified fleet card 105 miles west on Saturday night: "2011-08-20 22:15 — York, NE (Exit 353, 8 miles from Prairie Grain Co-op) — 26.4 gal Diesel, Fleet Card #004-SUTTER, PIN verified."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Sutter gave Fleet Card #004-SUTTER and his PIN to a farmhand or assistant manager who drove the Co-op F-250 on Saturday night while Sutter remained in Omaha.

2. CONTRADICTION (Hotel Room Occupancy Gap): Sutter's claim of continuous stay at the Cornhusker Marriott (doc04) conflicts with the 39-hour door-lock absence in doc08: "Keycard Lock Audit Room 614: Last entry 2011-08-19 18:04; zero door openings logged 2011-08-20; next entry 2011-08-21 09:40."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Sutter stayed in another guest's room at the hotel on Friday and Saturday nights, or the Room 614 battery-operated mortise lock clock/memory buffer dropped events until Sunday morning.

3. NEXT LEAD:
   - Pull CCTV and cashier shift records from the York, NE I-80 Fuel Mart for `2011-08-20 22:15` (doc12) to visually identify the driver of the Co-op F-250.
   - Re-interview Dale Sutter anchored to doc08 and doc12: "Room 614 shows zero keycard entries between Friday 18:04 and Sunday 09:40 (doc08), and Fleet Card #004-SUTTER was used with your PIN in York at 22:15 Saturday (doc12); who had possession of the Co-op F-250 and your PIN that night?"

DA Cold Case Intake — Case 2016-881 (Pelican Cove Marina Boathouse Shooting).
[doc01] Voluntary statement of charters captain Victor Lowe (2016-07-05): "On July 3rd, I took my sportfisher *Sea Wraith* out past the 12-mile reef at 16:00 for an overnight swordfish drift. We stayed offshore in international waters with the radio off until 07:00 on July 4th."
[doc06] USCG Sector Miami AIS Base Station Log (MMSI 367449120, Vessel *Sea Wraith*): "2016-07-03 23:12:08 UTC — Position 25.7741N, 80.1328W (Pelican Cove Turning Basin, 180 yards from Slip B-14), SOG 0.1 kts."
[doc07] Marina Shore-Power Smart Pedestal #B-14 Telemetry: "2016-07-03 19:08 EDT (23:08 UTC) — 50A Cord Plug-In Detected; KWh meter active until 2016-07-04 04:55 EDT."
What does the file show?

CASE BLUF: Coast Guard AIS transponder telemetry and marina shore-power meter logs contradict Victor Lowe's statement that *Sea Wraith* remained 12+ miles offshore overnight on July 3–4, 2016.

1. CONTRADICTION (Vessel Offshore Claim vs. USCG AIS Position): In doc01, Lowe claims, "On July 3rd, I took my sportfisher *Sea Wraith* out past the 12-mile reef at 16:00 for an overnight swordfish drift. We stayed offshore... until 07:00 on July 4th." In contrast, doc06 logs MMSI 367449120 inside the harbor at 19:12 EDT: "2016-07-03 23:12:08 UTC — Position 25.7741N, 80.1328W (Pelican Cove Turning Basin, 180 yards from Slip B-14), SOG 0.1 kts."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Lowe departed offshore on a second tender or buddy boat while leaving *Sea Wraith*'s AIS transponder powered on in the basin, or mechanical trouble forced an unlogged early return to the dock after which Lowe went home.

2. CONTRADICTION (Overnight Drift vs. Slip B-14 Shore Power): doc01's claim of an all-night offshore drift conflicts with doc07: "2016-07-03 19:08 EDT (23:08 UTC) — 50A Cord Plug-In Detected; KWh meter active until 2016-07-04 04:55 EDT."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Another transient vessel berthed in Slip B-14 and connected to Pedestal #B-14 while *Sea Wraith* was moored briefly in the turning basin or tended by a mate.

3. NEXT LEAD:

   - Interview any deckhands or charter passengers named on *Sea Wraith*'s July 3rd float plan and ask Lowe specifically about the 19:08 EDT shore-power connection in doc07.

Reviewing 1979-1120 (Starlight Lanes Night Manager Murder).
doc05 (Statement of Pinsetter Mechanic Gary Hollis, 1979-12-03): "I was snowed in at my cabin up on County Road 14 all night December 1st. Phone lines were down from the blizzard and my plow truck had a cracked distributor cap, so I couldn't budge till Monday morning."
doc09 (Sheriff's Tow & Impound Ledger, Shift 3, 1979-12-02 01:40 AM): "Winched 1974 Ford F-100 (Plate 79-G-4109, Reg: Gary Hollis) out of ditch at Milepost 2.1 on Old Mill Rd — 0.4 miles behind Starlight Lanes. Driver signed tow slip #1108 in person."
doc10 (Exemplar Comparison, Crime Lab Report #80-19): "Ink signature 'Gary Hollis' on Tow Slip #1108 exhibits concordant class and individual stroke features with known exemplars of Gary Hollis."

CASE BLUF: A contemporaneous sheriff's tow slip bearing Gary Hollis's handwriting-matched signature places him and his truck 0.4 miles behind the crime scene at 01:40 AM, contradicting his snowed-in cabin alibi.

1. CONTRADICTION (Inoperable Truck & Cabin Alibi vs. Roadside Winch-Out): In doc05, Hollis states, "I was snowed in at my cabin up on County Road 14 all night December 1st... my plow truck had a cracked distributor cap, so I couldn't budge till Monday morning." However, doc09 records on the same night: "1979-12-02 01:40 AM: Winched 1974 Ford F-100 (Plate 79-G-4109, Reg: Gary Hollis) out of ditch at Milepost 2.1 on Old Mill Rd — 0.4 miles behind Starlight Lanes. Driver signed tow slip #1108 in person." Furthermore, doc10 confirms the signature on Tow Slip #1108 "exhibits concordant class and individual stroke features with known exemplars of Gary Hollis."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Hollis replaced or taped the distributor cap earlier that evening to drive into town for supplies or private business unrelated to Starlight Lanes, slid into the ditch on Old Mill Rd during the blizzard, and concealed the trip out of fear of being falsely linked to his workplace's homicide.

2. NEXT LEAD:
   - Interview the Shift 3 deputy and wrecker operator who executed Tow Slip #1108 (doc09) regarding Hollis's clothing, demeanor, tire tracks, and direction of travel at `01:40 AM`.
   - Re-interview Gary Hollis anchored to doc09 and doc10: "Tow Slip #1108 (doc09) shows your 1974 Ford F-100 was winched out of the ditch 0.4 miles behind Starlight Lanes at 01:40 AM on December 2nd with your verified signature (doc10); why were you on Old Mill Road that night?"

Squad Review — File 2021-3390 (Mercer Garment Loft Strangulation).
Exhibit A (Recorded Interview, Cutting Room Foreman Leo Cho, 2021-05-14): "I left the 3rd-floor loft at 19:00 sharp on May 12th, took the Uptown 1 train to 181st Street, and played Xbox on my home Wi-Fi all night."
Exhibit F (MTA OMNY Tap Log, Card ending -4409 linked to L. Cho Apple Pay): "2021-05-12 22:34:19 — Entry Tap at 28th St Station (2 blocks from Mercer Garment Loft), Uptown platform."
Exhibit G (Microsoft Xbox Live Session Telemetry, Gamertag LeoC_88, Subpoena Return #9912): "2021-05-12 19:00 to 23:18 EDT — Account OFFLINE. First sign-in event at 23:21:04 EDT from residential IP 98.14.220.11."

CASE BLUF: Transit tap records and gaming console server telemetry create a 3.5-hour uncorroborated gap between 19:00 and 22:34 on May 12, 2021, contradicting Leo Cho's claim of departing the garment district at 19:00.

1. CONTRADICTION (19:00 Subway Departure vs. 22:34 OMNY Entry Tap): In Exhibit A, Cho states, "I left the 3rd-floor loft at 19:00 sharp on May 12th, took the Uptown 1 train to 181st Street." Exhibit F logs his payment device tapping into the subway three and a half hours later near the scene: "2021-05-12 22:34:19 — Entry Tap at 28th St Station (2 blocks from Mercer Garment Loft), Uptown platform."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Cho left the loft at 19:00 as stated but stopped at a nearby restaurant, bar, or off-the-books side job in the 28th Street neighborhood for three hours before boarding the Uptown 1 train at 22:34.

2. CONTRADICTION (Evening Xbox Activity): Cho's claim in Exhibit A that he "played Xbox on my home Wi-Fi all night" conflicts with Exhibit G: "2021-05-12 19:00 to 23:18 EDT — Account OFFLINE. First sign-in event at 23:21:04 EDT from residential IP 98.14.220.11."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Cho played an offline single-player campaign while his console was disconnected from Xbox Live, or he confused May 12th's gaming schedule with the prior evening.

3. NEXT LEAD:

   - Re-interview Leo Cho anchored to Exhibit F and Exhibit G: "Your Apple Pay OMNY log shows an entry tap at 28th St Station at 22:34:19 (Exhibit F) and your Xbox account first signed in at 23:21:04 (Exhibit G); where were you between 19:00 and 22:34?"

- doc12 (US West Local Exchange Toll Record, Timberline Motel PBX Trunk 208-555-2200): "1991-03-09 20:00 to 1991-03-10 06:00 — Zero long-distance or local calls originated from Room 9 extension (#109)."
- doc15 (US Forest Service Gatehouse Log, Road 42 Check Station — 1.5 miles below Blue Spruce Camp): "1991-03-09 22:40 — White Datsun King Cab (ID Plate 2B-8819, driver ID'd by gate guard S. Miller as Clint Ward) exited camp road southbound; chainsaw bar visible in open bed."

CASE BLUF: Telephone company PBX toll records and a Forest Service gatehouse log contradict Clint Ward's statement that he spent the evening of 1991-03-09 in Timberline Motel Room 9.

1. CONTRADICTION (10:15 PM Room Phone Call): In doc03, Ward claims, "I called my ex-wife in Boise from the room phone around 10:15 PM and went right to sleep." In contrast, doc12 establishes: "1991-03-09 20:00 to 1991-03-10 06:00 — Zero long-distance or local calls originated from Room 9 extension (#109)."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Ward placed the call using a coin payphone outside the motel lobby or via a calling-card access number that bypassed the Room 9 PBX extension billing log.

2. CONTRADICTION (Motel Presence vs. Forest Service Gate Sighting): Ward's claim in doc03 that "Me and my chainsaw stayed down in town at the Timberline Motel Room 9 the whole night of March 9th" conflicts with doc15: "1991-03-09 22:40 — White Datsun King Cab (ID Plate 2B-8819, driver ID'd by gate guard S. Miller as Clint Ward) exited camp road southbound; chainsaw bar visible in open bed."
   - INNOCENT ALTERNATIVE: Ward drove up Road 42 earlier to retrieve his personal chainsaw tools from a timber landing outside the bunkhouse area to prevent theft, or gate guard S. Miller misidentified the time or driver of a similar white Datsun pickup.

3. NEXT LEAD:

   - Interview USFS gate guard S. Miller regarding the `22:40` encounter in doc15 (whether Ward stopped to speak, road conditions, and exact lighting at Check Station 42).
